normative_action: Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code and organize by feature; do not introduce NgModules for ordinary feature development.
exceptions: NgModules when an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them.

normative_action: Keep structure feature-oriented: no application-wide technical buckets (global components/, services/, models/) or empty architecture folders; feature code inside its feature; core/shared small.
Keep pages/components focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.
Signals for synchronous local UI state, RxJS for async streams/HTTP composition/cancellation/event pipelines; avoid mechanical conversions.
Prefer simple component, signal or feature-service state before a state-management library.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services/HTTP boundary; no HttpClient calls scattered in presentation components; no backend Domain entities in Angular; use frontend API models matching the published contract.
Prefer functional interceptors for new code; interceptors stay cross-cutting and never contain feature business logic.
Follow the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing where practical; do not infer business behaviour from human-readable exception messages.
Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation, data integrity or security enforcement.
Avoid manual nested subscriptions; prefer composition operators when clearer.
Tie manual subscriptions from framework-managed code to the component/service lifecycle using current Angular facilities.
HTTP status codes/transport semantics belong to the API layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics (no blanket 200; 201 only when an API resource is created; no 202 for completed work); a 204 response has no body.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing/failed authentication, 403 for authenticated but not permitted; 404 hiding must be a deliberate consistent security policy.
409 for valid requests conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Keep status-code behaviour consistent across similar endpoints.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Cross-endpoint consistency obligation; oracle API policies define per-outcome semantics and stable error contracts but not consistency across similar endpoints.

normative_action: Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexistence of client generations creates a concrete need.

Once a version is relied on by external clients avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking change requires by default a new version or explicitly approved compatibility strategy; do not judge compatibility only by compilation.
Use one versioning strategy consistently; URL-segment (/api/v1/...) is default unless requirements justify header or query string.

Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important statuses incl. binding/validation/auth/rate limiting/central exception handling, schemas, auth); no speculative responses.
Enable Swagger UI in Development by default; expose elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic; no full business workflows or expensive/mutating database work.

Keep liveness and readiness distinct: liveness avoids external dependencies by default; readiness may depend on required capabilities and stays unhealthy until required startup work completes (never use liveness for that).
Publicly reachable health responses must not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary diagnostics.

Dependencies point inward: Domain depends on no other project; Application on Domain; Infrastructure on Application and Domain; Api on Application and Infrastructure only for composition/registration; inner layers never depend on outer layers; Domain/Application never reference Infrastructure-specific types.
If a feature seems to require an outward reference, reconsider the abstraction boundary instead of adding the reference.
Production reference graph: Domain→none, Application→Domain, Infrastructure→Application+Domain, Api→Application+Infrastructure; never Domain→Application/Infrastructure or Application→Infrastructure.
Backend test projects get no broader production references than their scope requires and keep inward discipline.

Test reference allow-list: Domain.Tests→Domain; Application.Tests→Application (+Domain as needed); IntegrationTests→Api (WebApplicationFactory<Program>); Infrastructure.Tests→Infrastructure (narrower as required).
Backend test projects follow the canonical set <Name>.Domain.Tests (optional), <Name>.Application.Tests, <Name>.IntegrationTests, <Name>.Infrastructure.Tests (optional).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Oracle constrains test references and location but not test-project naming/roles; this fixes a naming convention (also relied on by check-manifests).

normative_action: Keep Domain free of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities are default; CRUD/straightforward workflow rules are enforced in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed edits alone do not justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behaviour into Domain only when non-trivial invariants materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation independent of a use case; otherwise Rich Domain/DDD tactical patterns require explicit approval.
exceptions: Unless the approved specification already requires that design.

normative_action: Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar merely to appear domain-driven.
Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism; an oversized service is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not to introduce another pattern.
Define persistence and external-service abstractions in Application when use cases require them; keep infrastructure details out of Application.
Application must not use DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, provider-specific types or ASP.NET Core transport types.
Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin: bind/validate input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes to HTTP responses.
Do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Controllers must not contain business logic, access DbContext or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.
Program.cs is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.
Prefer specific repository interfaces for cohesive Application persistence needs over table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts.
Define repository interfaces in Application and implement them in Infrastructure.

Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, DbSet<T>, DbContext, EF expressions or provider types; LINQ-to-EF stays in Infrastructure; return materialized entities/collections/projections/result models.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T>/generic CRUD contracts; a generic repository/base class may exist only in Infrastructure to remove genuine duplication and must not become a replacement for EF Core queries; use-case queries live in concrete repositories.

IUnitOfWork (SaveChangesAsync) is the default commit boundary; repositories stage and do not call SaveChangesAsync; Application Services decide when to commit; Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork with the DbContext.
Repositories in one use case share the same Unit of Work and scoped DbContext; repositories injected explicitly; IUnitOfWork is not a repository container/service locator.
Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond SaveChangesAsync.

EF Core is an Infrastructure detail used with full capabilities inside Infrastructure; do not leak EF concepts into Application; do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.
Constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property injection.
Respect lifetimes; never capture a shorter-lived (e.g. scoped) dependency in a longer-lived service.
Registration near the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence/adapters, Api is the composition root.

Prefer strongly typed options, validate at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct/secure operation, avoid scattered string IConfiguration lookups (direct IConfiguration belongs to composition/registration).
When Serilog is configured use builder.Services.AddSerilog(...) rather than UseSerilog; keep provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code depends on ILogger<T>.
Keep cache technology out of Domain; do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; no HttpResponseMessage/remote transport concerns in Application.
Do not create separate Domain/persistence models merely for multiple API versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary when practical.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely for layer-shaped types; introduce transport contracts when separation gives a concrete boundary benefit.
Follow repository conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity; do not rewrite working code solely for newer syntax; consistency and readability over maximal feature use.
For new C# code prefer file-scoped namespaces (when consistent), one primary top-level type per matching file, Async suffix for Task/ValueTask methods.
exceptions: Small private/nested supporting types may stay with the owning type; Async suffix not required when an existing interface/framework contract makes it inappropriate.

normative_action: Do not rename established APIs solely to add the Async suffix; do not reorganize existing files merely for preferred member ordering.

Primary constructors fit DI or simple clear initialization; use a regular constructor when validation/initialization is non-trivial, explicit fields improve readability, the codebase uses that style, or parameter capture hurts understanding.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Constructor-style selection criteria; oracle (RUN-009, EXC-002/EXC-003) leaves constructor preferences outside the policy set.

normative_action: Do not convert constructors mechanically.

Use records when value semantics/immutability are desirable (many DTOs, genuine Value Objects) and classes when identity, mutable lifecycle, inheritance or framework behaviour fit; do not turn every DTO or Domain type into a record.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Record/class selection style rule not in the oracle (EXC-003 lists record preferences as outside it).

normative_action: Keep implementation details non-public unless part of the public API; use sealed to communicate deliberate non-inheritance, not as speculative JIT optimization.

normative_action: Use collection expressions, pattern matching, switch expressions, target-typed construction and other modern features only when they make code easier to read.
Use var when the type is obvious or unimportant; explicit type when it improves clarity.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Type-inference style convention outside the oracle.

normative_action: Use standard .NET naming (PascalCase types/methods/properties/public members, camelCase parameters/locals, meaningful names); private-field naming follows the repository convention.
exceptions: Private-field naming follows established repository convention.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Concrete naming convention not stated in any oracle policy (RUN-009 only defers to existing conventions).

normative_action: Use ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation in log calls.
Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked.
Avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-011 limits style rewrites outside the requested change; avoiding large formatting/modernization changes mixed into functional work within the change is additional.

normative_action: Adding, updating or removing a dependency follows the add-dependency workflow (version selection, due diligence, license approval).
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; no packages for hypothetical future use; 'approved' does not mean 'install by default'.
Use NuGet CPM: versions in Directory.Packages.props, PackageReference versionless by default, no duplicated versions in .csproj; keep each reference in the narrowest project needing it.
Use npm for the Angular workspace unless deliberately changed; maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json, keep the lockfile consistent; build/test tooling in devDependencies.
exceptions: Another package manager deliberately adopted; tooling in dependencies when there is a reason.

normative_action: Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable error contracts stable and safe; clients must not depend on human-readable messages.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid broad try/catch blocks that only log and rethrow.

Catch an exception only when the current layer can recover, translate it into its own abstraction-level outcome, perform a defined fallback, add context while preserving the original exception, or perform required cleanup.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-007 discourages repetitive catch/log/rethrow; a closed whitelist of acceptable catch purposes forbids any other catch (stricter than the oracle).

normative_action: Never expose stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secrets or sensitive exception details in public API errors.

Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when clearer (null, bool, typed outcome, deliberately adopted Result<T>) without forcing a generic Result<T>; Application categories use business semantics (NotFound, Conflict, Validation, BusinessRuleViolation) not HTTP names; expected outcomes are not logged as application errors by default.
Do not establish business exceptions as default architecture or throw/catch to jump between normal expected branches.

Use FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; API validates transport concerns, Application use-case rules, Domain owned invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions; do not move Domain invariants into validators or duplicate rules mechanically.
Log an unexpected exception once at the handling boundary; not repeatedly across repository, Application, Controller and global handler.
Normal client-request cancellation is not mapped to a generic 500 or logged as an unhandled failure.
External I/O calls have bounded execution time; distinguish per-attempt from total-operation timeouts; avoid overlapping unclear timeout mechanisms.
Retry only when repeating is safe; never auto-retry state-changing operations (e.g. POST/PATCH) without idempotency key, idempotent semantics or concrete deduplication.
Respect Retry-After or rate-limit guidance where appropriate; no indefinite/aggressive retries.
Use fallback only when semantically acceptable; do not hide correctness failures behind default values.
Caller cancellation is not a transient dependency failure; do not retry it or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
Prefer clear correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement/profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations.
Use async APIs for async I/O; never block with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async.
Propagate CancellationToken when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
Use TimeProvider for current-clock-dependent logic needing deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace stored/explicit timestamps.
Do not create/dispose HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.
Filter/project in the database when practical, avoid round trips/over-fetching/N+1, paginate potentially large result sets.
Caching is an optimization, introduced only for a clear measured/reasoned need; implementation chosen from deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the value incl. identifier, tenant, user, locale, query parameters; no global keys for user/tenant data.
Invalidate/update cache only consistently with successful mutations; cache is never a second source of truth.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or explicit invalidation strategy.
Introduce compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool, manual pooling, custom serialization optimizations, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for measured/demonstrated need.
Do not sacrifice maintainability for speculative micro-optimization.
For demonstrated allocation-heavy hot paths spans/pooling/source-generated serialization/preallocated buffers are appropriate; verify the optimization materially improves the workload.
Maintain a small deterministic representative seed dataset for an empty Development database covering meaningful states and relationships.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern; may use AppDbContext directly without Application repositories/IUnitOfWork.

Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder in Infrastructure (e.g. Persistence/Seeding/) exposed via a narrow initialization extension, not Program.cs, DbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in Development; never seed Production automatically.
Tests own their setup and never use the development seeder.
The seeder must not call Database.Migrate(), EnsureCreated() or create/upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.
If representative data exists leave it unchanged; no seeder-driven synchronization/repair/upgrade/overwrite/recreation; developers recreate the local database explicitly.
Seed entities preserve Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive/random combinations.
appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local SQL Server connection string when it holds no secret credentials; credential-bearing values via user-secrets or another approved local mechanism.

Do not create speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets; create a project/directory/shared area only with real cohesive code (no SharedKernel/BuildingBlocks/EventBus without requirement, no empty ValueObjects/ or Events/, no test project without concrete need).

normative_action: Never hardcode/commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings in source-controlled files incl. example configuration.
Use a local secret mechanism (dotnet user-secrets) in development and environment secret injection/managed secret store when deployed; do not assume a cloud provider unless chosen.

Treat data crossing the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploads, external responses, message payloads, user identifiers/filters) as untrusted and validate at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Do not trust client file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when handling/security depends on content.
Use parameterized database access (EF LINQ, supported mechanisms for raw SQL/Dapper/ADO.NET); never concatenate untrusted input into SQL.
Enforce authorization on the server; frontend guards/hidden buttons/client checks are UX only.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; no redundant [Authorize] when a secure global/fallback policy expresses intent.
Do not implement custom token/password security, hashing or reset-token crypto when ASP.NET Core authentication/Identity covers it.
For Bearer/OIDC validate issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority and lifetime per provider; never disable validation to make a token work.
Do not expose authentication-failure detail revealing secrets/account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks.
When browser cookies carry authentication include CSRF protection; an Angular frontend does not remove the risk.
Do not claim one browser token storage is universally secure; choose by threat model; never log tokens.

Production traffic with credentials/sensitive data uses TLS; respect hosting topology (in-app HTTPS redirection not required when the boundary secures transport); never disable certificate validation.
exceptions: In-app HTTPS redirection not required when TLS terminates at a proxy/ingress/gateway/platform.

normative_action: No custom cryptography when a reviewed platform mechanism fits; Data Protection is not universal database encryption.
Configure the narrowest CORS policy satisfying actual browser clients; never combine credentials with unrestricted origins.

Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, auth secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without permitted operational need; log level does not make data safe; prefer stable technical identifiers.
exceptions: PII when a concrete permitted operational need exists.

normative_action: Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log minimum useful non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization/permission/required-control checks fail safely rather than converting lookup/config failures into success.
Prefer visible startup/configuration failure over insecure fallback when a required security control cannot be configured.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (ASP.NET runtime image) not the SDK image; do not switch to root to bypass filesystem permission problems.
Security-sensitive dependency changes must not bypass dependencies.md and add-dependency (selection, versioning, licensing, vulnerability checks).
Use NUnit as default .NET test framework; no second framework without concrete reason.
exceptions: An established project deliberately using another framework keeps its convention.

normative_action: Choose the narrowest meaningful test level (unit for isolated logic, integration for wiring/HTTP/EF/persistence/serialization/auth/interaction); no fixed ratio.
Use WebApplicationFactory<Program> integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, auth, DI, repositories, EF Core or persistence must be proven.
Tests verify observable behaviour and survive refactoring; no dependence on private methods, internal call sequences, implementation classes; do not reproduce the algorithm.
exceptions: Interaction verification when the interaction is specified behaviour.

normative_action: For small finite input/state spaces prefer explicit declarative cases ([TestCase]) over loops, branches, LINQ, generated cases or computed expectations.
Prefer one observable scenario per test; a multi-step test only when the sequence itself is the behaviour.
exceptions: Multi-step test when the sequence is the behaviour.

normative_action: Tests are deterministic, order-independent, isolated from Production/Development data, uncontrolled external systems, wall-clock timing (use TimeProvider) and shared mutable state; never connect automated tests to Production data.
Tests start from a known state and own setup; no dependence on development seeding or other tests' order.
Use the actual provider when relational/provider behaviour matters; Testcontainers optional; no fidelity claims from another provider or EF InMemory.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage percentage.
Use descriptive test names communicating scenario/condition and expected behaviour.

why_extra_or_uncertain: TST-012 requires descriptive names but no specific pattern; the pattern is an added default.

normative_action: Resolve any SPECIFICATION/CUSTOM_SETTINGS conflict before changing implementation.

After approval record the setting in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md with a stable descriptive name, value and purpose.
Update owning code, validation, configuration, tests and externally relevant documentation for a new setting.

normative_action: When an approved value is added/changed/removed update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface; one changed literal does not establish synchronization.

Search for the old value/name, validators/DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, DB mapping constraints, frontend validation/UI hints, tests/test data, documentation/examples and mirroring configuration.
Separate occurrences expressing the setting from numeric coincidences and update only affected behaviour.

Verify settings changes: search stale references, build affected projects, run relevant tests, verify persistence, check SPECIFICATION.md for conflicts, run verify.
Direct IConfiguration access belongs to the composition root, provider setup and infrastructure registration; ordinary application services receive typed options.

Use keyed services only when implementations are selected by a known key; decorators when the same cross-cutting behaviour wraps an abstraction; assembly scanning only for genuinely repetitive registration and over the assembly that owns the services.

Inspect relevant existing code before any non-trivial change.

Read every rule whose paths match areas to be created or changed (explicitly for new files/greenfield, since path rules load only with matching files) and load knowledge skills for the technologies involved.
Classify open decisions with Decision Control; Reserved goes to architecture-decision before implementing that part.
If the request looks questionable raise the concern and an alternative before implementing.
Route sub-tasks: dependency changes to add-dependency, CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes to custom-settings, new projects/structural changes to project-structure.
When a new behavioural rule is approved update the durable source of truth (SPECIFICATION.md when appropriate; CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md via custom-settings for tunable values).

For a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence add a regression test that fails before and passes after the fix, unless equivalent coverage exists.
Performance-motivated changes: identify the bottleneck, preserve behaviour, simplest optimization, add/preserve tests, benchmark/profile non-obvious or complex optimizations.

Before declaring implementation complete run verify at a depth appropriate to scope and risk.

An Infrastructure extension creates the scope and delegates to the internal DbSeeder; migration strategy is separate from seeding.
